findings.where: First screen, the action row: the blue 'Write to me' button and the underlined address 'Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com' beside it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The page's one personal way to reach Mark does nothing when clicked. The parts map lists both 'Write to me' and the address as static. The button looks like a button and the address is underlined like a link, but neither opens an email. On the first screen, the only link that works is 'Book a consultation'. The working email link is in the footer, five screens down.
findings.who_objects: A development bank officer who arrives ready to write to Mark. They click the obvious button or the address, nothing happens, and the page looks broken. They either copy the address by hand or leave, which defeats the job this first screen is for.

findings.where: First screen, the action row: 'Book a consultation' beside 'Write to me'
findings.fault: The first screen asks for two actions instead of one, and the second has nothing behind it. 'Book a consultation' links to #consult, which no section on the page answers, and there is no booking system. The wording is also the sales funnel of a firm with a calendar, not one advisor saying 'write to me'.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the brief asks for one direct, personal action and calls 'salesy' a failure. The visitor, because they must choose between two blue buttons that look equal, and the one that works goes nowhere. Mark, because a booking pitch makes his advisory practice look like a retail service.

findings.where: First screen, the three blue margin notes (Istanbul 2025, Melbourne 2026, São Paulo 2024)
findings.fault: The only proof on the first screen can't be checked. The notes are in link blue, but the parts map lists all three as static, so a reader can't open the talk, slides or programme behind them. They read as links and lead nowhere.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader who checks specifics before shortlisting an advisor. They click a talk title to confirm the venue and content, nothing opens, and an unverifiable claim lowers trust in the rest of the page.

findings.where: First screen, the upper-case first-person paragraph ('I advise multilateral development banks, development agencies and governments…')
findings.fault: The paragraph claims the right kind of client only as categories. It names no body Mark has worked for, no role and no region of work. There is also no outside proof anywhere on the page: no named clients, no bodies that asked for or published his work, no testimonial. The only named institution is the university where he lectures.
findings.who_objects: A development bank officer who selects an individual against terms of reference. They need to see that he has done this kind of work for organisations like theirs, in their region, and a list of client types any consultancy could write does not show it.
